correctness.rationale: For a selected set with shore sizes a,b and c selected matched pairs, the total shortest-path length budget is k(k-1)-ab+2c, k=a+b. It is less than n(n-1) for k<n, and also for mixed k=n when n≥5 since ab>2c. A full shore at even n would need n/2 endpoint pairs at each omitted vertex, more than the total number of shore pairs. At odd n, on indices modulo n, assigning {i,j} to omitted index (i+j)/2 constructs the near-one-factorization and covers everything. For k=n+1, a mixed set with a,b≥2 omits c-1 matching pairs and leaves (a-1)(b-1)-(c-1) edges with both endpoints omitted. Each can only be the middle edge on a geodesic of a selected matched pair. Thus (a-1)(b-1)+1≤2c≤2min(a,b), impossible for a+b≥7 and a,b≥2. Finally for even n the chosen full shore plus b_0 works: the near-one-factorization on the odd index set excluding 0 covers the remaining neighbors of each b_t except a_0; one deranged assignment of pairs {a_0,a_j} supplies those omitted edges without duplicating a pair or using a forbidden edge. Edges at b_0 use direct paths. This proves both minima and the claimed complete optimizer families in scope; choosing additional unused pairs if required cannot spoil coverage.
residual_risks: The independent exhaustive shortest-path/cover replay at n=3,4 gives (minimum, count)=(3,14),(5,32), including 24 mixed-shore minima at n=4. The deposited n=5–7 checks and MILP were not independently replayed; the universal proof, not finite feasibility, establishes the claimed n≥5 families. No formal or expert verification is claimed.

evidence: The complete multipartite result characterizes all qualifying sets by omissions confined to one part with cardinality at most R_i. For K_{n,n} this gives n+1 for even n and n+2 for odd n, consistent with Klavžar–Zmazek.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A crown for n≥5 is not complete multipartite: the nonadjacency of a_i and b_i and of a_i and another a_j does not make b_i and a_j nonadjacent. In particular the diameter-two argument prohibiting omitted endpoints in different parts no longer applies. This is not specialization to another list of part sizes.

evidence: The supergraph K_{n,n} has the same even optimum and optimizer shapes, but has a different odd optimum. The proof of the complete multipartite criterion relies on all shortest paths having length at most two. Matched selected crown pairs admit length-three geodesics that can cover omitted-to-omitted edges.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Deleting edges affects the paths available as shortest paths, not just the number of edges to cover. The prior prohibition on omitted endpoints in two different parts cannot simply be carried across the deletion; crown rigidity needs the middle-edge capacity bound. Likewise, in an all-geodesics edge cover a single matched pair in a crown with n≥3 can use a whole family of length-three routes, unavailable to the strong convention. That comparison is mathematical, not an assertion about an inaccessible paper's text.

evidence: The exact strong-edge crown result in the retrieved index is the assigned finding itself. Gledel–Iršič Theorem 3.2 studies the same graph with one path per pair but vertex coverage. The indexed ordinary geodetic crown polynomials instead allow coverage of vertices by all shortest paths.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Covering vertices is not equivalent to covering edges. A length-three path between selected matched crown vertices can cover two omitted vertices and still leave all their other incident edges uncovered. Nor can many geodesics for a single pair be substituted for one chosen geodesic.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the standard one-perfect-matching deletion from the balanced complete bipartite family. The exact minimum detects a parity-sensitive effect of that deletion, while complete rigidity answers the more restrictive question of which endpoints an optimal cover can use. The number of eligible matching pairs controls the new length-three capacity; this explains why extra shortest paths do not produce mixed-shore minimizers once n≥5. This is a structural result rather than a recomputation of the complete bipartite minimum.
residual_risks: No classification for arbitrary matching deletions or all feasible sets of larger size is established.
